utterances.text: Now, there are a number of names contained in this document, and I'd like to ask you about several of them. The reference to -- in the second line in the English version, "Terzic's order," do you know this person Terzic?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Also on the first page --

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The interpretation came very late, and I interrupted it. Could it be repeated, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know this person Terzic that's referred to in the document?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Approximately seven lines down -- or nine lines down there's a reference to Serif Patkovic. Do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I know Serif Patkovic. He was a brigadier in the 7th Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Approximately halfway down the document there's a reference to Emir Mahmut Karalic. Do you know Emir Mahmut Karalic?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I do, as one of the commanders from the 7th Muslim in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: There's also right after the name Mahmut Karalic it says: "Chief Asim Koricic." Do you know who that person is?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I just know of Asim, who was a commander of the Muslim forces in Zenica. I don't know if that is this same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I ask now, since this document's already in evidence, that the witness be shown PT01032. That's 1032 in the binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What exhibit number is PT1032, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: 1032 is not yet in evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh. I thought you said, "Seeing it's already in evidence."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The prior document was Exhibit 121. So there's no need to tender that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Hamad, have you now had an opportunity to read this document?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Tell the Trial Chamber what this document relates to, please.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: It relates to the same attack on Visoko in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution would ask this document be admitted into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 319.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Hamad, several times today you've mentioned the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. Can you tell the Trial Chamber the relationship, if any, between the foreign Mujahedin and the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: There was a link and cooperation between the foreign Mujahedin and the 7th Muslim -- or, rather, when an attack was being planned, foreign Mujahedin and the 7th Muslim would be there. And the command of the 7th at the beginning of the war made it possible for foreign Mujahedin to have their own premises in the school in Zenica where the 7th Muslim was billeted until there was a misunderstanding between the 7th Muslim and the Mujahedin because of the killing of two foreign Mujahedin in the building in which the 7th Muslim Brigade was billeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And the killing of these two Mujahedin in the school, was that in any way related to combat?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: No, it was not related to any combat, but according to the best of my knowledge the decision was taken by some people who were not in Bosnia that Mahmut Karalic had to be liquidated, so that four foreign Mujahedin were engaged, and they were told that they had to be constantly present at the school in Zenica in order to liquidate Mahmut Alagic [as interpreted]. Two of the mentioned four who were intended for this liquidation, out of unknown reasons to me broke into Mahmut Karalic 's office. They were armed, and we could hear a lot of noise and shouting between them and Mahmut Karalic, and the bodyguards of Mahmut Karalic opened fire on the two Mujahedin and killed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I just need some clarification, because at one point again in the English interpretation we heard the name Mahmut Alagic. Was this assassination contempt concerning Alagic or Karalic?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Mahmut Karalic. Maybe I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask now with the assistance of the usher that the witness be shown the document that's been marked P02945. That's 2945.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Hamad, I would draw your attention, sir, to the right-hand part of this chart where there's reference to "Guerrilla." Do you see that in the document?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And underneath the box "Guerrilla," it would appear to be two subgroups, "Guerrilla G" and "Guerrilla P." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, first of all, let us establish what this document is, whose document it is, and how it relates to this witness, because as we have just heard, the witness was not a member of the 7th Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, first of all, the document speaks for itself in terms of the stamp contained on the upper-left corner. It appears to be an OrdBat of the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade. The witness has talked about -- or used the term "guerrilla," and I simply would ask him, if he -- if he's in a position to, to comment on what is contained in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may respond. The witness mentioned the Turkish guerrilla and not the guerrilla. Of these may be two quite different things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: They -- they may indeed, and that's precisely why I would ask the witness if he is in a position to comment on that. That's the precise reason I'm showing him the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, shouldn't you at least establish some kind of basis by way of relationship between the witness and the document even before you start asking him about the "Guerrilla"? At least whether he -- he recognises what this is and what -- you know, some kind of relationship between the document and the -- and the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I can certainly attempt to do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you may, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Hamad, were you aware of the structure of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Not too well, but I do know something about the guerrillas mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this, sir: This Ordbat that you see before you, I take it that you've never seen something like this in 1992 or 1993 or 1994 or 1995. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, again it's not so much an issue of this particular document, but the witness has indicated that he does have some knowledge about this particular unit, and the Prosecution would submit that it's relevant and has probative value to the ultimate issues for the Trial Chamber to determine. I don't know if the Defence continues in -- with respect to their objection, but I would ask the witness to explain his prior answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll find out whether the Defence still in its objection. You carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's just find out something here, Mr. Hamad. Did you, independent of this document, know anything of the structure of the 7th Mountain -- Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we didn't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The witness said, "No," if I understood the Bosnian language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you need this document to ask the witness about guerrillas?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. We'll withdraw the document in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: -- front of the -- of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned to us earlier that in the second Visoko operation the Turkish guerrilla were involved with the 7th Muslim Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us if there were any other units that you're aware of that went by the term "guerrilla"?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I don't know, but allow me to explain this a little. As far as the 7th Muslim Brigade in Zenica is concerned, I visited them on several occasions in the school in which they were billeted before I became a commander. I also visited them after the attack on Ilijas at the end of 1992. For a while I was wounded, so I was staying with them. I had occasion to talk to Brigadier Serif Patkovic. I also had occasion to talk to several members of the same brigade. And through these conversations with Serif Patkovic, the brigadier, and other soldiers, I learned that included in the same brigade were Turkish guerrillas. These Turkish guerrillas were not billeted in the school where the 7th Muslim was billeted, but they were in contact when it came to joint actions or attacks. The Turkish guerrillas were accommodated in the music school in Zenica, as I mentioned earlier on. This was a different school, so as to avoid all confusion. And the Muslim forces were in a school close to a barracks where other units were staying. So if an attack was being organised, the guerrillas would appear in the building of the 7th Muslim Brigade, and they would take part in the attack under the control of the 7th Muslim. I would also like to mention the fact that I met members of the Turkish guerrilla by chance in the facilities of the 7th Muslim Brigade. And I think that the document you showed to me a moment ago, it is true that I don't know anything about it, but I can assume when mention is made of the "Guerrilla" that the reference is to the Turkish guerrilla. And proof of this is that they took part in the attack on Ilijas in 1992, and I can confirm that there were Turkish guerrillas who appeared within the 7th Muslim Brigade. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: To your knowledge, sir, apart from the Turkish guerrilla were there any other guerrillas that you may have been aware of within the 7th Mountain Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not aware of any other groups known as guerrillas, but talking to Patkovic Serif, I know that they had battalions. They had companies. As for the guerrillas, I didn't hear of any others except the Turkish guerrillas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I just have a couple of questions on another subject that I think we can cover before the next break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Hamad, can you tell the Trial Chamber how the foreign fighters were able to communicate with the local soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Upon our very arrival in Bosnia of course we didn't know the local language, but there were several local people amongst us who could speak Arabic, and amongst us Arabs and Bosniaks there were people who could speak English. So that is how we communicated, using Arabic and English. There is something else. Amongst us foreign Mujahedin, from the beginning of the war men of Arab origin were included who had studied here in Bosnia. So they could speak both the local language and Arabic. And we used them as interpreters until we ourselves learnt the local language when we started communicating with members of the BH army in that language.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And final question before the break. Do you recall the names of any of the persons who spoke both languages, both Arabic and Bosnian, whether the person was an Arab or a Bosnian? Do you remember names of people who spoke both languages?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: For instance, among the Bosniaks there was Zuhdija Adilovic and the hodza from Travnik, Nusret Efendija. Then there was a Bosniak whose name I don't know, but we called him Abu Malik. Among the Arabs there was Souhail Tafiya. There was Abduladil Maqtauf phoen] that we sometimes used as an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When did you first learn to speak the Bosnian language, Mr. Hamad?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Until mid-1993 -- by mid-1993 I was able to communicate personally with commanders of the BH army without an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note the time, and for the benefit of my learned colleagues from the Defence, I would expect that following the break I would need about 30 minutes and then we should be in a position to start the cross-examination before we stop for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll take a break and come back at 1.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Hamad, did there come a time when the situation between the forces of the ARBiH and the HVO deteriorated?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: From what I know, it happened twice. Once during the attack on Ilijas in 1992, but I can say that the situation deteriorated more among the Bosniak units rather than between the army and the Mujahedin. And the second time was after the killing of the two Mujahedin where the 7th Muslim Brigade was billeted in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We spoke earlier today about check-points, and my question for you, sir, is did you ever become aware of any problems that the Mujahedin had at check-points aren't by the HVO? In 1993.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Before the conflict broke out between the BH army and the HVO we didn't have any problems rather than that we had to show documents or passports, but after the conflict broke out between the ARBiH and the HVO we had a lot of problems when going past the mentioned check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say after the conflict between the HVO and ARBiH had began, can you tell us approximately when that was to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I can say that the beginning of the misunderstanding was when we were at Karaula, because the BiH army after the fall of Jajce accused members of the HVO that they cooperated with the Serbian forces and that they had agreed to leave the Karaula without putting up resistance, so that the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which was not organised, was not I'll to put up resistance on its part. I know that I was in Bijelo Bucje as the unit commander when this was an armed conflict between the B and H army and the HVO, and I can say that the main reason was the presence of foreign Mujahedin in that area. I don't have information about things in other areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what kind of problems do you remember happening at HVO check-points with respect to the foreign Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: In which area exactly are you thinking of?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The -- in Central Bosnia, in the Lasva River valley or the Bijela -- Bijela valley?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: The problems were mostly because the HVO banned the Mujahedin from passing through their check-points, and the Mujahedin then had to pass through those check-points in order to have contact with the B and H army. So in 1993, even they would fire at our fighters. They would arrest them and detain them in Busovaca near Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Hamad, any of the foreign Mujahedin who were arrested and detained by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I know about a number of foreign Mujahedin who were in prison in Busovaca. For example, Abu Ali. He was from Kuwait. I don't know his real name. Abu Djafar from Egypt. I also don't know his real name. Then Abu Bukhari from Tunisia. He was captured by them too. Abu Ma'iz from Saudi Arabia. There were a few men that I know of, but perhaps at this point in time I cannot recall their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask with the assistance of the usher that the witness be shown the document that has been marked as P01059. That's 1059.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I would ask the witness please take a moment to read through this document. Have you finished reading both sides that have document, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Oh, there is something on the back as well. I'm sorry, I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Hamad, do you know about any of the situations described in this report?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't have any comments. Among the names that are mentioned in the document are a few names that I know, of persons who I know were detained by members of the HVO in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would ask that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 320.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask now that the witness be shown the document marked PT01056. That's 1056.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I would ask, Mr. Hamad, again this is a relatively lengthy document. I'm interested only in the first three paragraphs on page 2. If you could please read the first three paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the Prosecutor demonstrate a connection between the witness and this document. I would be very grateful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm simply going to ask the witness if he is aware of what's described in the first three paragraphs of this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And are you -- will you be -- by so doing, be establishing the connection between the witness and that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Simply we would use that as a basis for some questions about the document and as a foundational basis for tendering the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's hear what you've got to say. Madam Vidovic will stand up if she still has an objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that the Prosecutor would first need to establish a connection between the witness and the document and then expect an answer from the witness. How can the witness comment on this bulletin and on the 306th Brigade, which has not been mentioned so far, which is actually mentioned in the first three documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think Madam Vidovic has got a point, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps if I'm allowed to ask the witness a question then it -- we either can take the objection farther or perhaps see what -- what comes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Let's do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Hamad, have you read the first three paragraphs of this document?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I didn't manage to read everything. I stopped while the Judge was deciding if I should read the entire three paragraphs or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask, Your Honours, that the witness be given the opportunity to read the first they paragraphs, and then I'll put a question or questions to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine. You may proceed. You may proceed to read, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Hamad, are you familiar with the events that are described in the first three paragraphs of this document?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We'll withdraw the document, Your Honours, and I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is withdrawn. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Hamad, do you know of a place called Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: During the time period, sir, that you were in Central Bosnia in 1993 were you ever in that village?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes. While travelling to and from Mehurici and Travnik and at the end of the attack on Guca Gora in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say, sir, the attack on Guca Gora in 1993, do you recall the approximate time period when that attack took place?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber where your unit was in the few days before the attack?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I was in command of the unit which comprised 109 men. It was located in Bijelo Bucje. Also, we had enough of our foreign fighters in Mehurici who were ready for attack. Between me and the Mujahedin and the command in Mehurici there was no contact or communication other than radio connections, because the B and H army and the HVO were already in conflict at that time. So I could go from Bijelo Bucje only up to Travnik, and then I couldn't go further to Mehurici and Zenica because I had to pass through mountains where there were Croat villages and where the HVO was located. These places included Guca Gora. In cooperation with the B and H army, my unit, just like all the other units that were billeted in Travnik, were all issued an order to clear the terrain from Guca Gora up to Travnik of all Croats, both soldiers and civilians. And the Mujahedin who were in Mehurici, as well as other units of the B and H army, including Zenica, were given the assignment of clearing the terrain from Mehurici up to Guca Gora. We did that at the same time, so that I went from Travnik and Bijelo Bucje, and the Mujahedin from Mehurici joined up in Guca Gora, meaning that the road was completely cleared of all citizens of Croat ethnicity, both soldiers and civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And during these combat operations, Mr. Hamad, where did your unit go, through which villages?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: With the agreement of my first boss, Wahiuddin El Misri, and then with Mehmed Alagic, my task was to attack some six Croatian villages between Bijelo Bucje and Travnik. So I was supposed to end up in Travnik. That was the end of the work. Of it was not in my jurisdiction to move further towards Guca Gora and onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us then, Mr. Hamad, why it is that shortly after that attack you went to Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Because I was summoned by my chief, Wahiuddin, who personally organised and participated in the attack personally on Guca Gora. I was in Travnik, I had completed my assignment, and I was expecting a new order, what to do then, whether to return to Bijelo Bucje or to continue. In the meantime, I received a call from Wahiuddin when Guca Gora was captured that I urgently needed to go to Guca -- Guca Gora and that I needed to do this alone. Not with the unit but alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did Wahiuddin tell you why you needed to come alone to Guca Gora on that day?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: It was not our practice to ask the person in command why. An order was an order. It had to be carried out, no explanation necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Hamad, do you recall how long after the fighting had ended you went to Guca Gora pursuant to these orders of Wahiuddin?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I'm afraid that if I speculate or guess I might make a mistake. I don't know specifically how long we waited, was it a couple of days or 10 days. In any event, it was a very short period.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, where did you go in Guca Gora after being ordered to that location by Wahiuddin?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I went to the village. In the centre of the village there was a very large church. I didn't find Wahiuddin there, although he was there, but Guca Gora is not that small. He was in a different location. I encountered some Mujahedin who had led the attack, and then I encountered many foreign Mujahedin and many more Bosniak soldiers. And I think I also found General Mehmed Alagic. I cannot remember quite exactly. Perhaps he arrived immediately after I arrived at Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And on that day, sir, did you go into the large church in Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I did enter the church. That was completely demolished. Everything in the church was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you see, Mr. Hamad, any people in the church when you entered it? I found many foreign Mujahedin that I knew. For example, Saber [phoen] from Algeria; Adnan, I think from Egypt. I also found El Misri Imad, the commander. Abu Assadiqi from Algeria. Later also I met Wahiuddin, but not in the church but next to the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, with the assistance of the AV booth, I would ask that the witness now be shown a short video clip from PT6149. That's PT6149. This is an approximately two-minute clip. I would ask you to take a look at this, Mr. Hamad, and then I will ask you some questions about what we're about to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Hamad, do you recognise what was depicted in the video clip that we just observed?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: That is the church after the attack on Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise, sir, any of the people that were shown on that videotape?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Since the footage is bad, you couldn't really see all that well. I was able to recognise two people, Dr. Abu Haris from Libya, and Wahiuddin El Misri from Egypt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And at that point in time, sir, in 1993, can you tell us what positions were held by Dr. Haris and by Wahiuddin?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: At the time the first head of the Mujahedin, Ebu Abdul Aziz, was not in Bosnia. He left earlier. And Abu El Haris was a general chief of all the Mujahedin in Bosnia, and Wahiuddin was his deputy and an expert for all the Mujahedin military questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you comment, Mr. Hamad, on the condition of the church in Guca Gora as depicted in this videotape in relation to what you told us earlier that you observed there?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Before I reply to that question, I have to note something so that I don't forget. I saw Dr. Abu Haris and Wahiuddin on the footage but not in the church but next to the church. I also want to say that the footage of the church -- in that footage the church still looked neat, all right. So when this documentary was filmed, I was not present. When I got to Guca Gora, there was considerable chaos in the church already. In response to your question, I found the Mujahedin. They were already preparing to blow the church up. They were already placing certain quantities of TNT inside, at the corners, and in different places, the weak points of the building from the inside. And from outside they were also connecting them to some form of fuses. They called me, and they asked me if I had enough quantities of explosives, because they didn't have enough to blow up the church since the church was really big, with thick walls, about a metre thick.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And after you arrived and there came a time when you saw Wahiuddin, did he explain to you why he had summoned you or ordered you to come to Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: No. He didn't give me any specific orders. Wahiuddin is not the first person I came across in Guca Gora. After the scandal around the church where Mehmed Alagic was there, I saw Wahiuddin later, and he said that the church shouldn't be destroyed as this could be used as a reason to deteriorate relations between the Mujahedin and the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Hamad, did you hear or were you present at any discussion between General Alagic and Wahiuddin in Guca Gora on that day?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I was not, but I was present during the conversation between General Mehmed Alagic and one of the Mujahedins who were leading the attack on Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, what was the topic of that discussion?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I said that when I arrived at Guca Gora and I reached the church, I came across the Algerian Ebu El Sadik, and I repeat that he was one of the persons who was leading the attack. He was not a foot soldier. Also when I reached the spot, I can't remember whether Mehmed Alagic was already there or whether he came immediately after I arrived. I just know there was a debate over the church. Of there was a quarrel and a lot of impoliteness between the general and Ebu El Sadik. The general saw what was happening in the church, what the foreign Mujahedin intended to do, and he prohibited this. But before that, he asked about Wahiuddin in order to talk to him. And Sadik retorted quite angrily and said that he -- they could only talk to him. And then it became so serious that El Sadik almost killed the general, and the general then went back to Travnik. I just remembered that the general threatened that if we did blow the church up that they would attack us with other units that were part of his corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hamad.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the video clip that we just observed be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we do that, I've got a question in relation to that clip. Mr. Hamad, you testified that when you got there fuses were being put, preparations were being made to blow up the church, and they asked you if you had any more fuses because they didn't have enough to blow the church. The question I'm going to put to you, you're not obliged to answer if you feel like it's incriminating you, and the question is: Did you give them the fuses that they asked for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They didn't ask for fuses. They asked for explosives, that is TNT to be specific, and I answered that I didn't have it. So I didn't give it to them because I didn't have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Okay. The clip is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, Exhibit number 3211.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Hamad, you told us early this morning in response to some questions about Afghanistan that you had joined al-Qaeda. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, are you still a member of that organisation?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I can say that I worked for that organisation until 1997, which means when I was arrested in 1997, up until that time I was actively involved with al-Qaeda. Now, of course, I am no longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber why you're no longer active in that organisation?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I'm now in prison since 1997, which means that I have spent almost 10 years in prison, and I realised that this happened because of them. I considered them to blame for ending up in prison. To be quite honest, even before my prison term I realised that keeping company with such people can only lead to death or imprisonment. But I joined the al-Qaeda ranks beyond -- they were reasons beyond my will. In trying to explain why I joined the al-Qaeda and why in 2001 I was excluded from the same, and I wrote a book of 1.000 pages about this, and it is really difficult for me to explain this in a couple of sentences, because this story is as long almost as my whole life.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, Mr. Hamad, why you're serving a gaol sentence?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Because of my active --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is the relevance of that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would expect, Your Honours, that it might go to the witness's credibility and would be the basis of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may answer the question, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am in prison because of terrorist activities in this state up until 1997. Actually, I was charged of activating a car bomb in the western part of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Hamad, at any point in time since you received a prison sentence has any part of that sentence been reduced?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes, on two occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please explain to the Trial Chamber why your prison sentence was reduced on those two occasions?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Let me first explain that I became a dangerous terrorist for many people and a danger to the environment according to the judgement of the Supreme Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I was sentenced to 12 years and 9 months without any right to pardon or to be released on parole, but nevertheless my sentence was reduced twice. And to this day, I am wondering why, because in the judgement it says that this could not happen. The first time the sentence was reduced by eight months as a former member of the BH army. This occurred in 1998 when the former president of Bosnia and Herzegovina allowed collective pardon for all persons who were imprisoned throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina. Those who were not members of the army or the military police or the HVO, their sentences were reduced by four months, and those who were members of the army, the military police, or the HVO, their sentence was reduced by eight months. And I was one of these people whose sentence was reduced by eight months. So they recognise, and they have a document showing that I was a member of the BH army. The second time my sentence was reduced by six months - this was in 2004 - on the basis of an appeal I addressed to President Nikola Lozancic, and in this appeal I explained that I had been a member of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and this explanation was accepted so that my sentence was reduced by six months.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions for the witness at this time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Before I begin the cross-examination of this witness, I wish to ask Your Honours to allow me a little more time than the Prosecution used for the examination-in-chief, because not only will I refer to the questions put by the Prosecutor during his examination, but I believe that the witness knows and can answer many questions relating to the Defence case, and I will to a significant degree be dealing with questions relating to the credibility of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, madam. We'll see how reasonably longer than the Prosecution your time is, and we'll determine it as we go along. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I shall do my very best to be as brief as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness. Before I start my examination, I just wish to tell you the fact that the nature of the cross-examination is such that you can answer most of my questions very simply with a yes or no. As I wish to put a large number of questions to you, I beg you to give me brief answers and to provide your own comments only if I ask you to do so or if Their Honours so require. Have you understood me?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. You have just told us that you have written a book of a thousand pages; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You call it "International Terrorism and al-Qaeda: I've Finally Come Out of the Darkness Into the Light."

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is your confession about the events, including those that took place during the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have provided a copy of that book to the Prosecutor of the International Tribunal who copied it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 15th of August, 2006, you made a statement to the investigators of this Tribunal; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you signed it?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I made my statement to The Hague investigators twice, the first time in 2005, and then in 2006, and I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your additional explanation. So you signed both of those statements?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I signed the second statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this is the one dated the 15th of August, 2006; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You presented events truthfully in your book, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you wrote a book on the basis of your own knowledge and to the best of your recollection; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You wrote the book because you had decided to fight against terrorism and hatred on a religious basis?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes, it is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You repented because of everything that was done on a religious basis; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes. And I no longer wish to live in darkness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I now wish to ask you a few questions relating to you personally. Tell us, please, your name once again.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: My name is Ali Ahmad Ali Hamad.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was your father's a name?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: My father's name is Ahmad.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is the maiden name of your mother?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I don't wish to answer that question, because I believe that is my private affair. This is painful childhood that I had with my family. I had a large number of problems with them, and that is why I don't wish to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is quite unusual. I'm asking a very simple question, for the witness to tell us the maiden name of his mother.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If Your Honours believe that to be important, I will answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic, the witness has identified himself quite sufficiently. He told us his names, his full names. What's the relevance of asking that question which he says is painful, it reminds him of a painful childhood?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the question is relevant because I'm trying to ascertain the personal data about this witness, and it is highly relevant for the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But if the witness then says he does not wish to answer the question, what can we do about it? Do you want to force him to answer the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't, Your Honour. I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, Witness, where exactly were you born? You said you were born in Bahrain. Would you tell us exactly where you were born?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I was born in the capital of Bahrain, Manama.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. What kind of school did you complete, if any?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I completed my secondary education in Bahrain, biology, and because of my very difficult childhood in my family home I skipped a year, and then I attended the military academy abroad.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you did not complete your secondary education.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite right, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In answer to the Prosecutor's questions you said you had completed your secondary school.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: When I talk about my private affairs I don't go into any details, but you can see that in my book I speak about the details, and I supplied The Hague Tribunal with copies of this book on two occasions, so they were familiar with the details.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You're testifying under oath today. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in answer to a question from the Prosecution you said you had completed your secondary school; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes. But I mentioned earlier on when the Prosecution asked me whether I had missed a year, I said I had, and this is contained in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you tell us, please, when you got married, Witness, what year?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when was your first daughter born?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please tell us all the nicknames that you used during the war in Bosnia --

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: In addition to Abu -- Abu Aicha, and they also called me Alija. Nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us exactly when you went to Gradina?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: It is hard for me to tell. If you're asking me to give you dates and months, I cannot do it. But I can tell you that it was in 1992 and September. That is as much as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when did you go to Bijelo Bucje?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: That is even more difficult for me to answer. I said it was a couple of months after that. Whether it was two or three months later, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And how much time did you spend at Bijelo Bucje?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I think I was there for about half a year. A little more or a little less.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you tell us where you were during 1994?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I mentioned that I abandoned the Muslim forces and the Mujahedin for a while, and I joined various Bosniak units, and this was for a short period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes, I was in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I left Bosnia during the war once.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when that was?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: This was in 1994 exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And how long did this period last when you were absent?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I know I returned to Bahrain to renew some documents. I don't know exactly how much time I spent there, but I know it was a brief visit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you assist us in telling us when you returned to Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: The same year, but when exactly and which month I don't recollect.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that you were a citizen of Bahrain; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wish at this point in time to show the witness a document. D314, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you will see this document consists of two pages. Will you please look at the first page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is in English. This is the second page. Could the first page of the English version be shown for the witness first, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, is that a copy of your identity card?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now will you look at the second document, please.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I'm familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from being familiar, is this a copy of your driving licence?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could please documents be given an exhibit number and admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The documents are admitted into evidence. May they please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 322.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. I wanted to ask that those documents be tendered under one exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They have been admitted under one exhibit number. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to ask you something else. Sir, today receiving you mentioned several times the al-Qaeda organisation, and I would like to spend some time on that topic. I would like to put some questions to you relating to that organisation because I believe you could answer them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if at this point the witness could look at document D316.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I think that you have the document in front of you. It's document D316.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, I would like to say -- or for the recording, I would like to say that this is a document of the regional court of the United States court, State of New York, and it's the indictment against Osama bin Laden.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like you to look at this document. I would like you to look at the list of the accused. You can start from page 1. Since you said that you were a member of this organisation, do you recognise or do you know any of these names?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, can you refer us to the English part of this document? What pages must we look at? There are a number of pages.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's the first page of the English translation. The second page as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you know any of these names?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: As far as the place where it says Osama bin Laden, then Sheik Osama bin Laden, then Abdulah. It's one person. Actually, that is Osama bin Laden. I know the name of Abu Hafez El Misri. He's mentioned twice. Abu Haz El Misri [phoen]. And then three times Abu Haz El Misri El Kadra [phoen]. I think that is one person, the same person. And I know this person from Afghanistan. As for the others, they're not familiar to me other than Dr. Ayman al-Zawahiri, but I just know that having heard of it, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You already told us that you met Osama bin Laden. Did you meet any of these other people that you said you know them?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes. Abu Hazelas Misri [phoen], I met him as I was -- when I was just a regular soldier in al-Qaeda.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I would like to ask you to look at page 6 of this document. It's page 6 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is page 3 of the English version, and then also goes over into page 4. The send of page 3 and going into page 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you need to look at page 6.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Should I read the whole thing?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to draw your attention to the text around the middle of the page so that we don't -- we save some time, and it all begins: "In the course of 1991, the leadership of al-Qaeda, including their Emir, or prince, the accused Osama bin Laden transferred to Sudan. Al-Qaeda was based in Sudan from approximately 1991 until approximately 1996 but still maintained offices in various parts of the world." Please, is this what you also know about al-Qaeda, that it was headquartered in Sudan at this time?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: That is not correct. It was headquartered in Afghanistan where it was properly organised, but because of the pressure on the Taliban, Osama bin Laden left Afghanistan and went to Sudan.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that it had offices in different parts of the world?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I know about some places where they had their people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you to look at page 7 in the Bosnian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that is page 5 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention, Witness, to this part: Look at article -- or paragraph 5. That's all I'm interested in. In paragraph 5 it says -- it's at the end. Can you please look at this part? I'm going to quote: "Al-Qaeda functioned both -- in both ways, both on its own and through some of the terrorist organisations that operated under its umbrella, including the Egyptian Islamic jihad and at times the Islamic group also known as Al-Jama'a al-Islamiyya or simply Jama'at, led by Sheik Omar Abdel-Rahman and later by Ahmed Refi Taha [phoen], aka Abu Jaser al-Masri," and so on and so forth. Can you please also look where many jihad groups are enumerated in different countries, including Bosnia? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Earlier I asked you about your book. Would you agree that you in your book in this way exactly described the activities of al-Qaeda?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes, but in my own way. I did it in my own way, but I completely agree with what you read out under paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I'm going to ask you now about the Egyptian Islamic Jihad, or Al-Jama'a al-Islamiyya, or al-Jama'at. You know about this organisation, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes. I am aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you to look at paragraph 6 of this document, which is on page 8 in Bosnian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's page 7 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please look at Article 7.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note we don't have that particular page of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it Article 6 or Article 7 you want to have -- look at, madam?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Article 7. Your Honours, I apologise. We will look at Article 6 first. I would like for the witness to look at paragraph 6 and then paragraph 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, can you look at paragraph 6. What I would like to ask you is simple. Did you know that al-Qaeda had a command structure that included the so-called Majlis al-Shura?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Majlis and Shura, those two words are not familiar to me. I did not use it in my contacts with Osama bin Laden and other important people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You never heard of Shura when you were in contact with al-Qaeda?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I only heard that here in Bosnia, just here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please now look at paragraph 7. It says that al-Qaeda also had a Military Committee which considered and approved military matters. Did you know that, since you claim that you were a member of al-Qaeda?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I don't know that. Even though I was a member of al-Qaeda it doesn't mean that I know everything about al-Qaeda.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you actually a member of al-Qaeda or an officer of al-Qaeda?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I was a member of al-Qaeda, and I was sent from Afghanistan and told that I would be at the head of a combat unit, and this is exactly what happened here in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand you. Were you an officer of al-Qaeda or not?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Here in Bosnia, yes. I was one of the officers of al-Qaeda.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document be given an exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 323.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to this document, I would like to show you another document on the same topic. Can you please look at D317. It's -- well, you told us that you wrote a book, and I would like you to look at an excerpt from that book. First of all, I would like to ask you to look at page -- Witness, when I ask you about your book, the easiest thing would be to follow these large numbers that you have at the top of the page. You have this long number, 06050299. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at this page, and can you pay attention to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where is that number written? Oh, 06050299. Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, can you look at the last section of this document. Of course the whole page is interesting, but what I'm interested in is the part where it says: "D. Italy." You -- and while we're on this page, do you agree that in your book you described activities of al-Qaeda in different states? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now I would like you to look at this it excerpt, what is written here, this part that concerns Italy. You wrote there: "Cheikh Enver Sha'aban and his group were in charge of the same job in Italy. Anyway, Enver Sha'aban and most of his guys are of Egyptian origin, and they belong to the Egyptian terrorist group Jama'at El Jihad al-Islamiyya. The mentioned organisation planned and carried out the attempted assassination of the current Egyptian president Anwar."

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Anwar El Sadat.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it's Anwar El Sadat that we're talking about. Now I would like to ask you if that is the same organisation that is mentioned in the indictment that you saw just a bit earlier against -- or versus Osama bin Laden.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document be given an exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 324.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On this same topic, Witness, I would like you to look at document 318. It's an excerpt from a book, "Al-Qaeda's Jihad in Europe," by Evan Kohlmann, and this is on page 59. Witness, you have the Bosnian and English versions here. I would like you to look at the excerpt on page 39, the bottom of page 39. The bottom of that page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in the English version it's the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, Witness, I would like to give you a short quote. Cheikh Enver Sha'aban is mentioned, and it says in the book: "Cheikh Enver Saddam [as interpreted] --"

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I just need to find that place.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The author is re-telling this testimony of a witness who said that he testified that Sha'aban personally helped that Pakistani visas be arranged for him and three other guys for jihad, who then went to a camp connected to bin Laden, also in Afghanistan, in order to learn how to use weapons and explosives. Proof compiled by United States and the Italian authorities indicates that these four were not alone and that Sha'aban was personally responsible for arranging the training of hundreds, of potentially thousands for training in al-Qaeda.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... please. I'm not quite sure where you are. I don't know whether you are reading from this document or -- and if you can move slowly, please, because -- and before you -- if you are going to read direct us clearly where you are reading from, because I've lost you now for the last couple of minutes. Can --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I quoted page 39 in the Bosnian version, and you have the second page of the English version which begins with the words "Similarly."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]... Chamber that when you referred, as you said, page 39 of the Bosnian, and then you said in the English it's similar, and there is no page number in the English. So we didn't know where you were. You have a minute until the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's page 2, Your Honours. I'm sorry. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you probably read the excerpts, and I just wanted to finish that. "The centre developed quickly under Sha'aban's leadership into a major hub in the network of Arab-Afghan activity in all of southern Europe." Now, on this particular excerpt I would like to ask you the following: Sheik Enver Sha'aban, which in this part of the book is described as the leader of the Islamic centre in Milan, is that the same Sheik Enver Sha'aban that you wrote about in your book? You answered "yes," did you not?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now, Witness, can you please look at page 3 of this document, this same document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is the next page in the English version in relation to the one that we just saw.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, your version is page 103 and you have it in front of you. Can you look at this part that begins with "Three months after the first meeting"? So: "Three months after the first meeting of Abu Talal's and al-Qasimi and Enver Sha'aban's European Shura Council, Italian law enforcement and intelligent officials grew concerned after intercepting a letter from a fundamentalist militant imprisoned in southern Italy. In the letter there was talk about possible terrorist attacks on US and French targets in the region." Now I would like to ask you this: Did you ever hear about the European Shura Council?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I would like you to look at another excerpt of Evan Kohlmann's book. Of it's on page 4 of this exhibit. If you can please look at it. This is page 101 of the book.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in English it's the next page. It begins with the word, "Thus only months after," and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to briefly quote from this. "Thus not even a year after the commencement of hostilities in the Balkans the Arab-Afghan notion of heroically saving Bosnia's threatened Muslim population was already taking a back seat to the primary goal of using Bosnia as the springboard for a greater and more expansive international holy struggle. "Even as fierce battles continued between the Serbs and Muslims for control of Sarajevo, Sheik Abu Abdel Aziz Barbaros left the region on a major fundraising jaunt across the Middle East. Barbaros sought to collect large sums of money, especially from wealthy Arabian Gulf donors, spread word of the jihad in Bosnia and explain the situation to the scholars." Please, what you described in your book, does that correspond to what Mr. Kohlmann describes in his book? Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes, I did, but I would ask you to clarify that in a different way.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You don't understand the question?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: No, I didn't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to put it more simply. This that is written in the excerpt from the book that I read to you correspond to what you know about the objectives of al-Qaeda in Bosnia and that Bosnia is a springboard for a wider struggle?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Basically, yes, but there are more details here that I did not mention. There are things in this book that I didn't know. There are more details here that I didn't mention in my book, but in essence it talks about the same things that I talked about.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let's clarify. You knew that the al-Qaeda interest in Bosnia was much broader than just helping Bosnian Muslims.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD
utterances.text: Yes, I knew about that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document be given an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 325.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And, Madam Vidovic, would that be a convenient point?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll take an adjournment and reconvene tomorrow in the same court at half past 9.00. Court adjourned.
